title: Minimal formal coordinates and residual Jacobian minors
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge2$, $T=F[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Put $R=T/I$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n/I$, $t=\dim_F((I+\mathfrak n^2)/\mathfrak n^2)$ and $e=n-t$. Let $J$ be the ideal of $(n-1)$-minors of $(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)$ over $R$ [def-weil-matrix, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], with derivatives as in [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. There exist $g_1,\ldots,g_t\in I$ and $z_1,\ldots,z_e\in\mathfrak n$ whose linear terms form a basis of $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$, such that substitution gives an $F$-algebra coordinate isomorphism $F[[G_1,\ldots,G_t,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e]]\cong T$, sending the variables to $g_i,z_i$. In these coordinates put $h_j=f_j(0,\ldots,0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_e)$, $S=F[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_e]]$, $\mathfrak p=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_e)$ and $H=(h_1,\ldots,h_s)$. Then $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_t,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$, $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, and the induced complete local $F$-algebra isomorphism $R\cong S/H$ identifies the classes of $Z_i$ with an $F$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Under this isomorphism $J$ is the ideal $D$ defined as follows: $D=R$ if $e\le1$; if $e\ge2$, $D$ is the ideal of $(e-1)$-minors of $(\partial h_j/\partial Z_i)$ over $S/H$, and $D\subseteq\mathfrak m^{e-1}$. Minors of a size exceeding the number of rows or columns generate the zero ideal.

proof.text: The coefficient identification gives $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\cong F^n$. Choose a basis of the subspace $(I+\mathfrak n^2)/\mathfrak n^2$ and lift its $t$ members to $g_1,\ldots,g_t\in I$. Extend this basis to one of $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ and lift the remaining $e=n-t$ members to $z_1,\ldots,z_e\in\mathfrak n$. Thus their combined list has length $n$ and the required linear terms. Basis selection and extension are finite-dimensional linear algebra.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof: elimination of linear equations and identity/residual Jacobian block; Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined)

proof.text: The power-series regularity theorem makes $T$ Noetherian local of dimension $n$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and residue field $F$. Apply local Nakayama to the finite $T$-module $\mathfrak n$: the chosen classes span $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n\mathfrak n$, so $(g_1,\ldots,g_t,z_1,\ldots,z_e)=\mathfrak n$. The list is therefore a regular system of parameters by its definition. The full-coordinate theorem gives the $F$-algebra isomorphism $\phi:F[[G,Z]]\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. It and its inverse preserve the respective maximal ideals and hence every power, so they are continuous for the maximal-ideal topologies.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof: elimination of linear equations and identity/residual Jacobian block; Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined)

proof.text: Write $\widetilde f_j=\phi^{-1}(f_j)$ and $h_j=\widetilde f_j(0,Z)$. Assign each monomial containing a $G$ to its first such variable and divide by that variable; the resulting coefficient families give $\widetilde f_j-h_j=\sum_{a=1}^tG_aq_{aj}$ with $q_{aj}\in F[[G,Z]]$. Since every $G_a$ maps into $I$, this proves both inclusions in $\phi^{-1}(I)=(G_1,\ldots,G_t,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$. Moreover, the linear term of every $f_j$ lies in the span of the linear terms of the $g_a$. Thus the linear term of $\widetilde f_j$ is a combination only of the $G_a$, and setting $G=0$ leaves neither constant nor linear terms. Grouping each monomial of degree at least two by its first two variable factors shows $h_j\in\mathfrak p^2$; hence $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof: elimination of linear equations and identity/residual Jacobian block; Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined)

proof.text: Evaluation at $G=0$ has kernel $(G)$ by the same monomial grouping, and inclusion of $F[[Z]]$ is its section. Consequently the quotient maps induce mutually inverse $F$-algebra maps $T/I\cong S/H$. Both are local and preserve all maximal-ideal powers. The power-series theorem and the complete-local-quotient theorem apply to $T,I$ and $S,H$: both ideals are proper because they lie in the respective variable ideals. Hence this is an isomorphism of complete local $F$-algebras. Since $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, the quotient of $\mathfrak p/H$ by its square is exactly $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$; the coefficient identification gives its $F$-basis $[Z_1],\ldots,[Z_e]$. This is the required basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof: elimination of linear equations and identity/residual Jacobian block; Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined)

proof.text: Use fixed-size Jacobian-minor invariance, first for the parameter system $(g,z)$ of Step 2, then for the finite generating list $(G_1,\ldots,G_t,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$ of Step 3. It follows that $J$ is the ideal of $(n-1)$-minors of $B=\operatorname{diag}(I_t,A)$ over $S/H$, with $A=(\partial h_j/\partial Z_i)_{j,i}$. Indeed the derivative definition gives the identity matrix for the $G$ rows, zero $Z$ derivatives there, and zero $G$ derivatives for the $h$ rows, since these series involve only $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof: elimination of linear equations and identity/residual Jacobian block; Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined)

proof.text: If $e\le1$, then $t\ge n-1$, so choosing $n-1$ matching rows and columns in $I_t$ gives determinant $1$ and $J=R$. Suppose $e\ge2$. Adjoin all $t$ identity rows and columns to any $(e-1)$-minor of $A$; the block determinant formula gives that same determinant as an $(n-1)$-minor of $B$, so $D\subseteq J$. Conversely choose an $(n-1)$-minor of $B$. If its selected identity-row indices and identity-column indices differ, a selected row or column is zero. Otherwise these index sets agree, of size $a\le t$, and its matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(I_a,A')$, with $A'$ a $q$-minor of $A$ and $q=n-1-a\ge e-1$. The block formula identifies its determinant with $\det A'$. Repeated application of $J_{r+1}(A)\subseteq J_r(A)$ puts this determinant in $J_{e-1}(A)=D$. Thus $J=D$. If the residual matrix has too few rows for an $(e-1)$-minor, the same argument makes all the original minors zero.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof: elimination of linear equations and identity/residual Jacobian block; Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined)

proof.text: For $e\ge2$, each $h_j$ has no monomials of degree zero or one. The coefficient formula for its partial derivatives therefore gives $\partial h_j/\partial Z_i\in\mathfrak p$. Every summand in the determinant of an $(e-1)$-submatrix is a signed product of $e-1$ entries, hence belongs to $\mathfrak p^{e-1}$ and has image in $\mathfrak m^{e-1}$. Their sums and the ideal they generate have the same containment, proving $D\subseteq\mathfrak m^{e-1}$. Empty generating families give the zero ideal as stipulated.

Step 1: cotangent coefficient isomorphism plus basis lift from I. Step 2: power-series theorem (Noetherian, local, dim n), Nakayama on the finite module n, the definition of regular system of parameters, then the 07NM F-algebra coordinate isomorphism. Step 3 (elementary): (G)-division gives phi^-1(I)=(G,h); linear terms lie in G since f-sum c g lies in n^2=phi((G,Z)^2); h in p^2. Step 4: evaluation kernel (G) with section; quotient ideals proper (also e=0); p/(p^2+H)=p/p^2. Step 5: 0C4B invariance node used for coordinates and then for generators on F[[G,Z]] (generator count may change); derivative coefficients give the identity and zero blocks. Step 6: zero row or column when the selected identity index sets differ, otherwise diag(I_a,A'), block determinant, q in {e-1,e}, J_{r+1} in J_r; e<=1 identity minor 1; too-few-rows case handled. Step 7: Leibniz gives p^{e-1}. Small cases checked: (x1x2), (x1+x2^2), I=n, s<e-1, char p. Nearest DAG relatives (binary-hypersurface, hilbert-stratum-minors) are not duplicates.
